svg.title: From a Recurring Problem to a Paid Commitment
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-problem-to-paid-commitment; chapter number: 1; title: From a Recurring Problem to a Paid Commitment; subtitle: Find existing demand, understand the work, identify distribution, and make a delivery promise you can honor.; caption: Rob Walling, Greg Isenberg, Fomin Unscripted, and founders featured on Starter Story describe complementary problem-selection checks.; assumptions note: These checks combine Rob Walling's outside validation, Greg Isenberg's task mapping, Fomin Unscripted's distribution-first approach, and Starter Story cases; they are not one founder's reported sequence.; note: Gil's Starter Story account reports $20,000 from 50 lifetime licenses before building Subscribr, with delivery promised in 60 days and refund access for two weeks after delivery.; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Find repeated pain; value: Step 1; detail: Rob Walling recommends identifying the problem rather than pitching the idea. Abhishek, on Starter Story, looks for dissatisfaction with established tools.; step: 02; label: Validate beyond work; value: Step 2; detail: Rob Walling warns that an employer can be uniquely dysfunctional. Check that outside customers share the pain.; step: 03; label: Separate judgment from mechanics; value: Step 3; detail: Greg Isenberg documents each task precisely and separates judgment from mechanical work before automation.; step: 04; label: Name the acquisition channel; value: Step 4; detail: Fomin Unscripted identifies where customers will come from before building. Brett Malinowski describes demonstrating the customer's desired outcome in content.; step: 05; label: Price the delivery commitment; value: Step 5; detail: Gil's Subscribr pre-sale includes delivery and refund commitments. Screenshot One's founder, on Starter Story, raises prices and reduces free usage after the early $7 offer leaves almost zero margins.
